guideTitle: Best Generator Transfer Switches with Interlock (2026)
metaDescription: Five generator transfer switches built around a mechanical interlock or double-throw action that keeps utility and generator power apart, compared.
expertTake: The HKJWUN 32 amp dual switch is the pick when you want a described one-piece mechanical interlock in a sealed IP65 box. The Powants 20 amp unit is the value pick for a single furnace or freezer. Anyone looking for a panel-slide interlock kit for a main breaker panel should skip this list, because the data here contains none, and those kits are panel-specific.
introParagraphs: An interlock is a part of any transfer arrangement that makes it physically impossible for grid power and generator power to feed a home at once. It marks a safe changeover apart from a backfeed that can injure a line worker repairing storm damage.

Interlocks come in several forms: a sliding plate on a main panel, a double-throw lever in a disconnect box, or a mechanical link inside a small switch. Self-contained devices that do this job without being panel-specific are covered here, with a clear note on what each one does and does not protect.

products.name: HKJWUN 32A Dual Manual Switch with Mechanical Interlock, IP65
products.description:
HKJWUN describes its interlock as a one-piece mechanical design that physically stops utility and generator closing together, which is exactly the function this guide is about. The housing is rated IP65 with sealed cable glands and a transparent cover, so the switch position is visible without opening the box.

The 32 amp, 400 volt rating and the 12,000 watt figure place it above the 20 amp Powants unit and below the 100 amp Sekelo. It is a dual-source switch, so it serves one feeder, not a panel of selectable circuits. Specs like 400 volts hint at three-phase or industrial equipment, so confirm that your house is single-phase 120/240 volts before buying.

Plan on an electrician. A sealed IP65 box suits an outdoor wall, but cable gland sizing and wire choice depend on the feeder. Check the label for any certification, because the listing does not describe one in detail. In daily ownership the transparent cover is the feature you will use most: a glance tells you whether the box is on utility or on generator before you touch anything, and that habit prevents the classic mistake of starting a generator with the lever in the wrong position. Keep a small desiccant pack inside during humid seasons if the box lives on a coastal wall.
products.bestFor: Owners who want a visible, sealed, mechanically interlocked switch for one feeder.
pros: IP65 sealed box with cable glands
cons: One feeder only, no circuit selection

products.name: Powants 20A 125V ON-OFF-ON Interlock Transfer Switch

specList.label: Sources
specList.value: Portable or inverter generators, solar storage

products.description:
The ON-OFF-ON layout is the simplest interlock there is: the lever has a utility position, a generator position and an off in the middle, so it cannot sit in both. The listing says it works with portable generators, inverter generators and home solar energy storage.

At 1,800 watts it is a small device, the lightest-duty product in the guide. That is enough for a furnace blower, a refrigerator or a few lights, but not an air conditioner or a well pump. Against the HKJWUN, it gives up the sealed enclosure and the larger capacity and gains a much simpler install.

Copper prewiring helps keep terminations tidy. Pick one dedicated circuit, label it clearly and check that the generator's outlet and the cord match the 20 amp rating. Because the device is so small, it is easy to mount it somewhere that looks tidy but is awkward to reach in the dark, so choose a spot at chest height near the furnace and keep a flashlight hung beside it. A single device like this does not replace a plan for the circuits it leaves unpowered, such as water heating.
products.bestFor: Keeping one furnace, fridge or freezer circuit safely isolated from the grid.
pros: ON-OFF-ON lever cannot close both sources
Works with inverter and portable units

products.name: The Original EZ Generator Switch, Patented Manual Transfer

specList.label: Origin
specList.value: Made and assembled in the USA

products.description:
This is the product that defines its own name in the category. The listing calls it the original and patented EZ Generator Switch, made and assembled in the United States, and states UL, CSA and ETL approval. Those are seller claims, to be checked against the label.

The listing says little about electrical ratings or the mechanism, so you should read the manufacturer's instruction sheet before assuming how it interlocks. Compared with the HKJWUN and Powants, its appeal is brand heritage and domestic assembly instead of published numbers.

If you buy it, confirm the ratings against your generator and your panel before you commit, and ask the installer for the exact wiring procedure. A transfer device is only as safe as its installation. When the listing is this sparse, the manufacturer's installation sheet becomes the real reference, so download it before buying and show it to the electrician. If it describes an inlet, a breaker or a panel position that does not fit your house, you will know before money is spent. Support is the other half of the heritage story, since a maker who answers the phone is worth something in an outage.
products.bestFor: Buyers who prefer a long-established US-assembled switch and will verify ratings in the manual.
pros: Listing cites UL, CSA and ETL
cons: Few electrical numbers in the listing
Ratings must be confirmed in the manual
Mechanism is not described in the data

products.name: Sekelo 100A 120/240V Double-Throw Transfer Switch, 24,000W
products.description:
A double-throw disconnect is itself an interlock: one lever, two positions, never both. The Sekelo version is rated for 100 amps at 120/240 volts with a 24,000 watt listed capacity and aluminum connections in a galvanized housing.

It is a service-level box, hard-wired near the main panel. That puts it well above the small devices on cost, wire size and install effort, and it demands a licensed installer. The listing also draws attention to arc faults, reminding buyers that a disconnect handling this current is not a casual DIY project.

Aluminum lugs call for correct torque and compound. Look at the box annually, keep the cover closed and label the lever position for the household. A 100 amp unit is a sensible match for a sub-panel feeding a workshop or an apartment, where the generator is a mid-size standby unit rather than a portable. For whole houses on 200 amp service it is too small, and the Tzechkii is the better match. Never operate the lever under load unless the instructions say it is allowed.
products.bestFor: 100 amp sub-panel or service switching with a large generator.
pros: Double throw prevents both sources closing

products.name: Tzechkii 200A Manual Double-Throw Transfer Switch, NEMA 3R
products.description:
The Tzechkii is the largest interlocked switch here, matching a typical full-size residential service. Its manual lever moves between utility and an auxiliary source such as a gas generator, and the listing says the double-throw action prevents the two connecting at once.

The 48,000 watt capacity is the ceiling of the hardware, not a statement about what your generator can deliver. Next to the Sekelo, you get double the amperage and an explicit NEMA 3R rating for outdoor mounting.

It is electrician-only work. Service entrance connections can be lethal, a permit is typical and the utility may need to be told. Because the box sits outdoors, ask for a lockable cover or a padlock hasp, so an uninformed visitor cannot throw the lever. Pair it with a generator whose output is stable, since the switch passes whatever it receives straight to every circuit in the house.
products.bestFor: Whole-house service switching paired with a standby generator.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Interlocks come as a sliding plate on a main panel, a double-throw lever in a box, or an ON-OFF-ON handle in a small switch. The Powants uses the third, the Sekelo and Tzechkii use the second, and the HKJWUN describes a one-piece mechanical link. A sliding-plate kit is specific to your panel brand and model, which is why none appear here. Know which you need before you shop. If your main panel accepts a sliding-plate kit, ask the panel manufacturer for the approved part number rather than buying a generic plate, since a plate that does not fit your breaker spacing defeats the purpose. A small standalone switch, in contrast, works with any panel because it sits beside it.

The Powants at 20 amps and the HKJWUN at 32 amps switch one feeder. The Sekelo at 100 amps and the Tzechkii at 200 amps switch a whole panel. A single-feeder switch is cheap and easy to install but covers a single circuit. A service switch covers everything but needs an electrician and a big generator. The usual mistake is buying a service-sized disconnect for a household that only wants a refrigerator and a furnace powered, which turns a small project into a permitted one. Estimate your real load first, then match the tier to it.

A house in North America is normally single-phase 120/240 volts. The HKJWUN lists up to 400 volts, a figure that points to industrial or three-phase equipment, so confirm that its terminals, poles and layout suit single-phase household wiring before relying on it. Poles matter as well: a three-pole or four-pole switch used on a two-wire-plus-neutral house can leave a leg unswitched, which defeats the interlock's purpose. Ask the seller or the electrician to confirm the pole count in writing.

The HKJWUN is IP65 with sealed glands, the Tzechkii NEMA 3R. IP65 means dust-tight and resistant to water jets, and NEMA 3R is rain-tight but not jet-proof. Both are fine outdoors if installed correctly with conduit entering from below. The Powants and the EZ switch list no enclosure rating. Where no rating is listed, assume an indoor location and keep it dry. Even a rated box ages: gaskets harden, glands loosen and a box in direct sun can crack, so look at the seals each autumn.

The EZ Generator Switch listing cites UL, CSA and ETL approval. Those are seller claims. Check the label on the unit and ask the inspector what the jurisdiction accepts. An interlock that has not been approved for the installation may fail inspection or complicate an insurance claim.

Any device that connects a generator to house wiring is regulated electrical work, and service-level boxes are electrician-only in most places. A mechanical interlock prevents backfeed only if the rest of the wiring is correct. Ask your electrician and inspector before buying, and never rely on a homemade cord. A mechanical interlock is a protection against human error, and it is valuable precisely because storms and stress make people careless. It is not a replacement for a trained installer, a permit or an inspection.

howWeEvaluated.title: Interlock mechanism
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked for products that describe how the two sources are kept apart. The HKJWUN and Powants describe it, the double-throw boxes embody it, and the EZ listing is silent.

howWeEvaluated.title: Rating spread
howWeEvaluated.description: We covered 20, 32, 100 and 200 amp tiers so the guide serves a furnace, a feeder and a whole service. Ratings are listing statements.

howWeEvaluated.title: Enclosure and environment
howWeEvaluated.description: IP65 and NEMA 3R ratings were noted. We could not verify them, so they remain seller claims.

howWeEvaluated.title: Brand and documentation
howWeEvaluated.description: The EZ Generator Switch has the longest track record but the thinnest numbers. This tradeoff drives its placement. A reader who values a documented US-assembled switch will still find it a reasonable choice, provided the manual confirms the rating and the electrician is comfortable with it.

howWeEvaluated.title: Install burden
howWeEvaluated.description: A small ON-OFF-ON switch is a modest job, while a 200 amp disconnect is professional work. That burden shaped the picks. We also asked whether a first-time buyer could read the lever positions at a glance, since an interlock that confuses its user invites the mistakes it exists to prevent.

cards.label: Small switch
cards.text: The Powants and HKJWUN serve one feeder, install quickly and cost little. Limited to a single circuit's worth of load.

cards.label: Service disconnect
cards.text: The Sekelo and Tzechkii swap a whole panel. Powerful, but electrician-only and sized for big generators.

howToChoose.note: Choose a small switch for a few appliances and a disconnect only with a standby unit and a licensed installer.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A physical interlock or double-throw action that cannot close both sources, correct neutral and ground handling, and a documented install procedure.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The HKJWUN describes a one-piece mechanical interlock, the Powants an ON-OFF-ON handle, and the Sekelo and Tzechkii use double throw.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You need to switch a feeder with confidence in a sealed box, such as the HKJWUN, or a whole service with the Tzechkii.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: One furnace or freezer circuit is all you need. The Powants does the job.

maintenance.why: A stiff handle is a warning. Move it through each position with the generator off.
Gaskets harden over time. Replace a cracked seal or gland to keep the IP rating.
Aluminum especially loosens with heat cycles. An electrician should tighten to the label torque.
Damaged cords defeat the interlock's value. Replace anything with exposed copper.
A clear label tells family members which position is which. A laminated card listing the start-up order helps anyone who was not present at the install.

faq.q: Is an interlock the same as a transfer switch?
faq.a: An interlock is a safety feature within a transfer arrangement. A double-throw switch includes one by design, while a panel kit adds a sliding plate to a main breaker panel.

faq.q: Are panel interlock kits included here?
faq.a: No. Panel interlock kits are model-specific, and the data here contains none. Check the panel manufacturer for approved kits. Those kits exist for many popular panel lines, but compatibility depends on the exact main breaker, so a part number from the panel's own maker is the only dependable source. A standalone switch from this guide is the alternative if no kit is offered for your panel.

faq.q: Which switch is best for a furnace?
faq.a: The Powants 20A is aimed at one circuit up to about 1,800 watts, which covers a furnace blower. Confirm the circuit's breaker size first.

faq.q: Does an interlock make the install safe?
faq.a: It prevents dual feed, but wiring errors can still cause trouble. Neutral and ground handling matter, so use a licensed electrician. A correct install also includes a labelled generator inlet, a properly sized cord and a ground rod where the code requires one for a portable unit, none of which the interlock itself provides.
Most places require one for any generator tie-in. Ask the local authority.

faq.q: Can the HKJWUN's 400V rating be trusted for a house?
faq.a: A house is normally single-phase 120/240 volts. A 400 volt rating suggests industrial design, so verify poles and terminals before use.
